title: Keller monodromy is everything
W: Show every symmetric group appears as the hidden symmetry group of the fibres of some 3D Jacobian-conjecture counterexample.
M: Prove that for each $n\ge3$ there is a non-invertible Keller map $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ of geometric degree $n$ whose generic monodromy group is $S_n$.

title: Firebreak with wind
W: How long must a firebreak be to save a round town from a wind-driven fire?
M: For front speed $a+b\cos\theta$ and a disc town at distance $D$, find the minimal length of a curve built at speed $\sigma$ that protects the town.

title: Spikes at the primes
W: Put a fixed bump at every prime on the half-line lattice. Prove the electron is localized at energies inside the free band, as it would be if the primes were random.
M: Let $H=\Delta+\lambda\mathbf 1_{\mathbb P}$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$, $\lambda\ne0$. Prove that $H$ has pure point spectrum in $(-2,2)$.

title: Monochromatic square-sum triangles, many colours
W: Colour the positive integers with any finite number of colours. Show there are always three numbers of one colour whose pairwise sums are all squares.
M: Prove that for every $r$ and every $r$-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there are distinct $a,b,c$ of one colour with $a+b,a+c,b+c$ all perfect squares.

title: Computable connective constants
W: Count the self-avoiding walks of length n on the Cayley graph of a finitely generated group. Their n-th root tends to the connective constant, and upper bounds converge to it. For groups with a solvable word problem, is the connective constant always a computable number?
M: Let $G$ be a finitely generated group with solvable word problem and finite symmetric generating set $S$, let $c_n$ be the number of $n$-step self-avoiding walks from $e$ in the Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(G,S)$, and let $\mu(G,S)=\lim c_n^{1/n}=\inf_n c_n^{1/n}$ (so $\mu$ is upper semicomputable). Is $\mu(G,S)$ a computable real for every such $(G,S)$? If not, give a counterexample. If so, is it computable uniformly from $S$ and an algorithm for the word problem?

title: Four vortices on a square torus
W: Three point vortices on a flat torus are integrable. Show four identical ones are not.
M: Let $H=-\sum_{i<j}G(z_i-z_j)$, with $G$ the Green function of $\mathbb C/(\mathbb Z+i\mathbb Z)$, for four unit vortices. Prove that after reduction by the translation symmetry the system has no real-analytic first integral independent of $H$.

title: Hexagonal Lebesgue covering
W: Find the smallest convex shape that can cover every set of diameter 1, if covering is by translation only, not rotation.
M: Determine $\min\{\mathrm{area}(K):K$ convex, every set of diameter $1$ has a translate inside $K\}$, and prove the minimiser is unique.

title: Formal verification depth of RH
W: The Riemann hypothesis now has a Lean proof. Show it cannot be proved in a weak arithmetic like I-Sigma-1 plus exponentiation, or show it can.
M: Decide whether RH (as a $\Pi^0_1$ sentence) is provable in $\mathrm{I}\Sigma_1$, or in $\mathrm{EFA}$.

title: Heat with a cosine reaction
W: In u_t = u_xx + cos(x)u², the reaction averages to zero, but a second-order effect looks like +u³, the borderline Fujita case. Does every positive start blow up?
M: Prove or disprove: for every $0\le u_0\in C_c(\mathbb R)$, $u_0\not\equiv0$, the solution of $u_t=u_{xx}+\cos(x)\,u^2$ on $\mathbb R$ blows up in finite time.

title: Strauss exponent for an oscillating source
W: The wave equation with source |u|^p in 3D has small-data global existence exactly above the Strauss exponent 1+√2. Find the threshold when the source is multiplied by cos t.
M: For $u_{tt}-\Delta u=\cos(t)\,|u|^p$ on $\mathbb R^{1+3}$ with data $\varepsilon(f,g)$, $f,g\in C_c^\infty$, determine $p_c$ such that for $p>p_c$ solutions are global for all small $\varepsilon$, and for $1<p<p_c$ some data blow up for all small $\varepsilon$; decide whether $p_c=1+\sqrt2$.
